key_insight: Boron doping broadens the stability window of mixed-valence Cu-O phases, delaying oxidation to CuO and enabling much lower resistivity under oxygen-rich sputtering conditions.
engineering_relevance: The results provide a route to tune Cu-O thin films for optoelectronic and photovoltaic devices by controlling phase formation, defect chemistry, and electrical transport during deposition.
method: Reactive magnetron sputtering of Cu-O thin films with controlled oxygen partial pressure.
Systematic boron incorporation to probe changes in phase evolution and bonding.
Characterization of phase stability, chemical bonding, and resistivity across the deposition window.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a phase progression from Cu2O to Cu2O/Cu4O3 to CuO with increasing oxygen partial pressure, and highly B-doped films reached about 0.06 Ω·cm.
watch_item: The stabilization effect is demonstrated for specific sputtering conditions, so transfer to other substrates, thicknesses, or deposition systems may require re-optimization.
paper_title: Boron-assisted stabilization of low-resistivity mixed-valence Cu-O thin films prepared by reactive magnetron sputtering
